comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-RUS and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The coherent pathway selects the formal Politiek, geschiedenis en economie route: Soviet History and Memory and Russian Politics in year two, followed by The Russian Economy and Russian Foreign Policy in year three. The programme page frames the bachelor around understanding contemporary Russia and its political and economic developments, and the route is also first in the adopted OER and current curriculum. This selection is independent of UCR fit. The pathway preserves the full 30 EC genuine third-year elective space as two published 15-EC components and excludes the 0-EC thesis seminar, mentorship and non-curricular modules. Course EC were checked against the public 2026–27 module entries; the selected components account for exactly 180 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The current programme page foregrounds understanding contemporary Russia and its political and economic developments while retaining common Russian-language, historical and cultural foundations. This route therefore best represents the programme's broad academic identity and is also listed first in the current official curriculum; it was selected without reference to UCR fit.

exception.reason: Leiden’s 180-EC Russian Studies pathway combines a compulsory progressive Russian-language sequence with Russian history, literature, linguistics, politics and a study-abroad language component before advanced work in Soviet history, Russian politics, economics and foreign policy and a bachelor thesis. The selected pathway contains 70 EC of dedicated Russian-language acquisition, grammar, reading and linguistics. UCR offers no Russian-language course or Russia-focused disciplinary sequence. Its general history, politics, economics, literature and media courses can support comparative study, but they cannot implement a Russia-centred 24-course academic concept or the language-based source work central to the Leiden degree. A purported closest UCR Russian Studies alternative would rely on generic disciplinary neighbours and misrepresent the core.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026–27 BA-RUS study identifies a 60-EC first-year core, 40 EC of compulsory second-year work plus a 20-EC formal route, and a third year comprising a 20-EC continuation of that route, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine open elective space. The selected Politiek, geschiedenis en economie route contributes Soviet History and Memory, Russian Politics, The Russian Economy and Russian Foreign Policy. The OER confirms the two formal routes, a Russian-language progression with B2-level bachelor outcomes and the thesis prerequisites. The selected components preserve all 180 EC without counting the 0-EC thesis seminar or non-curricular modules.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The only Russian-specific mention is the Russian Revolution within GOSHIST111 Modern History’s broad 1815-to-present survey; the catalogue has no Russian-language course, no Slavic or Eurasian studies course and no Russia-focused sequence. GOSHIST111/211/312 provide modern, imperial and research history; GOSPOLI112/212/313 provide comparative politics, international relations and conflict; BENECON111/211/311/312 provide general economics and econometrics. MCCLITR111/112/311/312 and MCCMEDI111/211 offer general literary and media analysis, while HCBCOGN312 studies psycholinguistics rather than Russian. These courses cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Russian Studies rationale, supply progressive Russian proficiency or support Russian-language primary-source work, and no timetable can repair that substantive gap.
